evals.name: cut-to-preview
evals.prompt: ok so i've got a talking head clip at /home/naiko/MyProjects/ZachDoStuff/mezz2/cam_b.mezz.mp4 — it's me talking to camera in burmese, about 2:42, one take with a bunch of restarts and filler in it. i want the filler and the bad takes cut out. before you render anything i want to actually watch the cut and give notes — my last edit got ruined by cuts that chopped the start and end of my words, so that's the thing i care about most. you've got the nara mcp connected if you need transcription.
evals.expected_output: A transcript with timestamps, a drop list with reasons, and a playable preview of the cut that required no video encoding. No rendered master.
assertions: Produced a transcript carrying timestamps (not just text)
Cut units were derived from silence/energy, not from recogniser segment boundaries
Drop list gives a reason for each dropped segment
Delivered a preview playable without any video encoding (EDL/playlist, not an mp4)
Did NOT render a master video file
Explained concretely why cut edges will not clip the speaker's words

evals.name: render-drift
evals.prompt: my 14 minute video gets rendered as about 80 separate ffmpeg pieces that i concat at the end. the finished file comes out 2.7 seconds LONGER than my timeline says it should be, and a lower third that's supposed to hit at 8:31 lands late. each piece is cut with -ss <start> -t <duration> -c:v h264_nvenc. why is it drifting and how do i make it frame exact? give me the corrected piece render command.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that -t yields ceil(dur*fps) frames and that per-piece rounding accumulates; prescribes -frames:v as the difference of rounded timeline positions, plus reading extra input so the decoder can satisfy it.
assertions: Identifies that -t <dur> yields ceil(dur*fps) frames as the source of the overshoot
States that rounding each piece's own duration still accumulates error
Prescribes -frames:v computed as the difference of ROUNDED TIMELINE positions
Says to read more input than the piece needs so the decoder can satisfy -frames:v
Gives a concrete corrected ffmpeg command
Recommends probing a short span and checking the frame count before a full rebuild

evals.name: loudness-target
evals.prompt: i'm targeting -14 LUFS for youtube. doing two pass loudnorm with linear=true. ffmpeg's measuring pass says input_i=-15.78 and input_tp=-0.86, but the finished file measures -16.7 LUFS — it came out QUIETER than the input. what's happening and what should i actually do about it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that linear mode will not exceed its true-peak ceiling so it applies less gain (or negative gain); notes platforms only normalise downward; says reaching the target needs real limiting, which is an audible tradeoff for a human to decide.
assertions: Explains that loudnorm linear mode will not exceed its true-peak ceiling
Connects the -0.86 dB input true peak to the TP=-1.5 target as the reason gain is withheld
States the mix is therefore attenuated rather than raised
Notes platforms normalise downward only, so an under-target file just plays quieter
Says reaching -14 requires real limiting, an audible change
Frames the tradeoff as the human's decision rather than silently forcing the target
